sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Turbine-Driven Critical Care Invasive Ventilators

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–Hong Kong Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (signed 1965)
France–United States Double Taxation Avoidance Treaty (1967, as amended)
France–Germany Double Taxation Avoidance Treaty (1959, as amended)
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, Investment Chapter

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L561-1 to L561-56 and R561-1 to R561-55, as amended by the transposition of EU Directive 2018/843 (Fifth Anti-Money Laundering Directive); French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L820-1 to L820-33 and R820-1 to R820-11 (Register of Beneficial Owners); Decree No. 2017-638 of 27 April 2017 on the beneficial-owner register; EU Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers of funds; Order of 14 September 2011 on the AML/CFT program; General Financial Security Guidelines (Lignes directrices de l'ACPR); AMF and ACPR Joint Position 2014-16.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the corporate constitution (Statuts / Certificate of Incorporation) of each non-French corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official Companies Registry or Chamber of Commerce of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if originating state has acceded to the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961); otherwise Consular Legalization by the French Consulate in the originating jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Good Standing or equivalent official extract identifying directors and single beneficial owner of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority in the jurisdiction of incorporation (Companies Registry or equivalent supervisory body)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; alternatively Consular Legalization for non-Hague States

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Individual UBO identification documents — passport and recent proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issued by the UBO's national authority; address proof issued by municipal registry or public utility provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the passport certification / notarized signature; Consular Legalization if the UBO is a national or resident of a non-Hague Convention state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney concluded in favor of the French incorporation representative (porteur de parts) for the submission of pre-incorporation filings and name clearance steps
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent administrative authority in the constituent's home jurisdiction, countersigned by the local French notary if applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization) and, depending on the transaction, legalization by the French Consular Office

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance / criminal record extract (extrait de casier judiciaire) for each proposed SARL manager (gérant) who is a foreign national
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Police, Ministry of Justice, or designated criminal records authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all identified UBOs, proposed managers (gérants), and corporate shareholders against French national asset-freeze measures (Ministère de l'Économie), EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, UN Security Council sanctions lists (UNSC 1267/1989 and 1988 regimes), OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, and the GAFI/FATF list of amended jurisdictions. Persons identified as Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) trigger enhanced due diligence under Article L561-10 of the French Monetary and Financial Code, including verification of source of wealth and funds, reinforced hierarchy approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. The French ACPR and FIU (Tracfin) require filing of suspicious-transaction reports for any red flag, under Article L561-15 and L561-16 of the Monetary and Financial Code.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) maintained at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; preliminary name availability screening is performed through the INPI company name search portal (Data INPI / Recherche de disponibilité de nom)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French law mandates that the corporate name of a French SARL be expressed in French or contain a French-language element; any foreign language or script must be transliterated into Latin characters according to standard French orthographic rules. The name must not be misleading, contrary to public policy or good morals, or infringe prior trademark or corporate name rights. The words 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' must follow or precede the corporate name. Names implying a regulated activity or a public service are subject to prior ministerial authorization or sector-specific approval.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed corporate name by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce or upon third-party opposition to the name, the applicant may file a formal administrative appeal with the President of the Tribunal Judiciaire (commercial chamber) within one month from the date of notification, under Article L.235-4 of the French Commercial Code, seeking judicial cancellation of the competing name or an order allowing registration of the proposed name. The applicant may simultaneously initiate an opposition procedure before the INPI in accordance with the French Intellectual Property Code if the rejection is based on a conflicting earlier trademark. Where the rejection stems from a protected regulated term, the applicant must obtain the prior approval of the competent ministerial authority and resubmit the name in the same file. An extension of a name reservation is generally not permitted; the applicant must re-file a fresh name-request application if the initial 30-day reservation window lapses.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: In France, commercial domiciliation (virtual office / société de domiciliation) is permissible for administrative functions for a maximum cumulative duration of five years under Articles L.123-11 and R.123-4 of the French Commercial Code. However, for an ISIC 3250 manufacturer of critical care invasive mechanical ventilators, virtual office use is not permissible as the principal place of business because the company must maintain physical facilities, production equipment, quality-control systems, and regulatory documentation opening as required under French health law and the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR 2017/745). The ANSM requires a declared physical manufacturing site in France; thus, full commercial substance with an actual office, registered laboratory premises, and ventilators storage area is mandatory from incorporation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — approximately 85% likelihood of unannounced on-site inspections by the Agence Nationale de Sécurité du Médicament et des Produits de Santé (ANSM) and the Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) within the first 18 months of operation, especially in the ICU ventilator manufacturing segment, given the need to maintain ISO 13485 certification and French labor-code enforcement for production sites.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting of Articles of Association (statuts), corporate governance pass, and UBO-bank filing package by French avocat in wolf practice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per client engagement; statutory hourly or fixed advisory fees under the National Bar Rules (RIN)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of incorporation file and registration with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS entry)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official tariff under Decree No. 2020-1052 of 7 July 2020 (registrar tariff)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the statutory notice in a legal notices newspaper (JAL - Journal d'Annonces Légales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee regulated by the Ministry of Justice order on the tariff of legal notices

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Domiciliation service if a commercial registered office address is used during initial formation (virtual-office relay)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; under Articles L.123-11 and R.123-4 of the French Commercial Code the domiciliary must be be registered with the Police des Règlements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation (notarial or certified translator) of foreign corporate documents into French
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Court-approved tariff schedule for legal translations (arrêté of the Ministry of Justice)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague apostille / consular legalization fees for each foreign document (five documents in the bundle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority of the foreign state (apostille) or French Consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory fee per apostille or consular legalization act, varying by originating state; based on the Hague Convention certificate fee schedules

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank account opening with KYC and UBO verification process at a French licensed credit institution
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank fee schedule for commercial account opening and compliance due-diligence; no statutory cap

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary filing of a medical-device establishment declaration and intention to manufacture under MDR 2017/745 (ANSM pre-incorporation notice)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Agence National de Sécurité du Médicament et des Produits de Santé (ANSM)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: ANSMA regulatory fee schedule — no prep-incorporation fee applies; fees are triggered upon EU Declaration of Conformity

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 through L.223-43 and R.223-1 et seq. (SARL provisions); Regulation (EU) 2017/745 on medical devices applies to the business scope post-registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), administered by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered-office department; electronic filing through the Guichet unique des entreprises operated by INPI (formalities.entreprise.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form M0 – Déclaration de création d'une société commerciale, with annexed certified Articles of Association (statuts), deposit certificate, and proof of legal publication; registration culminates in the issuance of the official Kbis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for an SARL (Art. L.223-2, Code de commerce); capital amount is freely fixed in the Articles of Association. At least 50% of cash contributions (apports en numéraire) must be fully paid up at subscription and the balance within five years. All cash capital must be deposited into a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) with a French credit institution or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, releasable only after RCS registration. In-kind contributions are valued in the Articles; a contributions auditor (commissaire aux apports) is mandatory where any in-kind contribution exceeds €7,500 or the aggregate in-kind value exceeds half of the share capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE PARTNERS OF [■] SARL. The undersigned founding partners hereby RESOLVE: (1) the final Articles of Association are approved and ordered filed; (2) each founder's subscription is accepted and the share capital of EUR [■] is fully subscribed; (3) the manager certifies that all cash contributions are escrow-deposited at [■] and released only upon RCS registration; (4) the registered office is fixed at [■], France; (5) [■] is appointed Gérant with full authority to register, represent and bind the company; (6) the Gérant is authorized to sign the corporate registry form, publish the legal announcement, and complete all filings with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce until issuance of the Kbis.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the Articles of Association (Statuts) and ancillary formation acts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding partners under private deed (acte sous seing privé) or a notary (acte notarié) where an in-kind contribution comprises real property; no administrative authority at this stage.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the French-language statuts containing the mandatory information of Articles L.223-1 and L.223-7 of the Code de commerce: corporate name, business purpose, registered office address, share capital amount, allocation of shares, identity of partners, and particulars of the proposed Gérant. Execute the statement of formation acts (état des actes accomplis en vue de la formation). All partners must sign the statuts personally; at least 50% of cash contributions must be paid before registration. Ensure that in-kind contributions are properly appraised and recorded in the statuts.
required_dossiers: Draft / final Articles of Association (statuts)
Statement of subscription and payment of capital (état des actes accomplis)
Identity documents and tax residency evidence of each founder
Valuation report for in-kind contributions, where applicable
Declaration of non-conviction and intended Gérant consent letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the statuts are defective or incomplete, execute an amendatory agreement (avenant) countersigned by all partners before filing; notarized statuts require a supplemental notarial deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Escrow block of cash share capital (dépôt de fonds / compte bloqué)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC) or a French credit institution, holding the funds in the name of the company in formation ('[■] SARL en formation').
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the blocked deposit account in the corporate name, transfer the subscribed cash capital (in practice 100%, minimum legally required 50%), and keep the funds frozen until issuance of the RCS certificate. Obtain the official certificate of deposit of funds (attestation de dépôt des fonds) identifying the company, the amount deposited, the bank, and the blocked nature of the account. This certificate is a mandatory annex to the registration file.
required_dossiers: Company name and legal form declaration
Draft Articles of Association (statuts)
Passport or national identity card of the Gérant
Prospective registered office address evidence
Banking identification and account-opening requisites
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the deposit or issues a non-conforming attestation, transfer the funds to another institution or request a notarially certified deposit receipt; funds remain fully recoverable if registration ultimately fails.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the mandatory legal formation announcement (annonce légale)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved legal announcements gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales – JAL) in the department of the registered office, as required by Article R.223-8 of the Code de commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the French-language notice of incorporation (avis de constitution) to the approved JAL. The notice must state the corporate name, SARL legal form, registered office, share capital, business purpose, term, manager identity, and intended RCS registration. The publisher verifies the statutory content and issues the certificate of publication (attestation de parution / justificatif d'insertion), the original of which is annexed to the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Legal announcement text (avis de constitution)
Final Articles of Association (for the newspaper's verification)
Certificate of registered office department
Identity of the Gérant and signatory details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the announcement is inserted in a non-approved gazette or in the wrong department, arrange a fresh insertion in the correctly approved JAL and obtain a second attestation; the first publishing fee may be refunded at the publisher's discretion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the incorporation file through the Guichet unique and obtain RCS registration (Kbis)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (INPI portal, formalities.entreprise.gouv.fr), relayed to and processed by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce holding the RCS of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online M0 company-creation form, upload the full annex set in the order prescribed by French regulatory practice, and electronically sign the declaration. Pay the statutory greffe fee and ancillary taxes ideally via the portal's secured payment. The Greffe reviews legal compliance and registers the company in the RCS, automatically generating the Kbis extract bearing SIREN, SIRET, and APE/NAF 3250B, which evidences legal existence.
required_dossiers: Completed Form M0 (déclaration de création de société)
Certified copy of the Articles of Association (statuts)
Statement of subscription and payment of capital
Certificate of deposit of funds (attestation de dépôt des fonds)
Legal publication certificate (justificatif d'insertion)
Passport and proof of address of the Gérant
Signed declaration of the Gérant (non-conviction declaration)
Proof of the registered office occupancy (lease, ownership deed, or domiciliation agreement)
Receipt of fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Greffe may issue a regularization request (demande de régularisation) with a fixed deadline; submit the missing documents online within the allowed period. In case of final refusal, appeal before the summary-judge chamber of the commercial court (référé) or re-file a corrected application; blocked capital remains retractable until registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration compliance, Kbis retrieval, and downstream administrative activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS) and Infogreffe portal; INSEE, URSSAF, tax administration, and the competent medical-device authority (ANSM) for the regulated activity.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuance of the Kbis, verify the recorded APE/NAF code (expected 3250B – manufacture of medical devices and instruments); register with URSSAF and the corporate tax offices if employing staff or conducting chargeable operations; subscribe to professional civil liability and property insurance; open the definitive corporate bank account using the Kbis. As a medical-device manufacturer, initiate the ISO 13485 quality-management certification process and file the regulatory conformity dossier with ANSM and the relevant notified body under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 before placing the ICU ventilators on the market.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract and SIREN/SIRET notification
Professional liability and asset insurance policies
URSSAF employer-registration confirmation (if applicable)
Tax administration registration slip
ANSM/notified-body submission file for the medical device manufacturing activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the APE/NAF code is wrongly assigned, submit a correction request to INSEE supported by the Kbis; downstream environmental or health permits do not invalidate the RCS registration but must be secured before manufacturing starts, and any non-compliant commencement may trigger an administrative stop order from the DREETS or ANSM.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: ANSM (Agence nationale de sécurité du médicament et des produits de santé) for medical-device conformity and vigilance; DREETS / DRIEAT (Direction régionale de l'économie, de l'emploi, du travail et des solidarités) for industrial-site and environmental inspection (ICPE).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: I. CE Manufacturing Authorization under Regulation (EU) 2017/745: Annex IX Full Quality Assurance certificate (ISO 13485) and EU Declaration of Conformity for the recovered Class IIb life-sustaining invasive ventilator; II. Déclaration d'Installation Classée pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE) for the production facility, with the associated operating registrations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique, de la Biodiversité, de la Forêt, de la Mer et de la Pêche – Inspection des Installations Classées, exercised territorially through DREETS/DRIEAT.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: ICPE declaration (régime de la déclaration) under the applicable nomenclature rubric for light electronic/mechanical assembly and testing, or exemption (non classé) if below the declaration thresholds; full environmental impact assessment (étude d'impact) is not mandated for the typical ventilator assembly line, but an environmental compliance certificate is required by insurers and by the prefecture where thresholds are approached.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to the sanitary sewer must respect French limit values: pH 5.5–8.5, temperature ≤ 30°C, COD ≤ 125 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, TSS ≤ 35 mg/L (Arrêté of 2 February 1998); air emissions of VOC from cleaning or solvent use must not exceed 20 mg/m³ (hourly average) with a solvent label nearing zero ODS; hazardous wastes (solvents, electronic components, batteries, wiping materials) must be tracked by registered waste carriers, and waste manifests (bordereaux de suivi de déchets) maintained.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certification by SDIS (Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours) or the Commission de Sécurité where the premises are open to staff/public; structural load inspection certificate for cleanroom equipment and elevated storage; occupational clearance under the Code du travail comprising emergency evacuation plans, ventilation, periodic electrical verification, and mandatory employee medical surveillance; ISO 14644 cleanroom classification compliance for aseptic assembly if the ventilator patient interface demands controlled conditions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) and official portal impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French SARL entities obtain statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT ID by registering with INSEE for SIREN/SIRET number and filing prescribed forms with the local DGFiP tax office within 30 days of incorporation or activity commencement, supported by incorporation documents and proof of address.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Standard entity-level corporate taxation applies under the French Impôt sur les Sociétés regime; no check-the-box elections available; limited hybrid mismatch relief under EU directives only.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time e-invoicing and fiscal clearance under French law; API integration with certified platforms (e.g. PEPES) for digital stamping and immediate reporting to tax authorities; non-compliance triggers fines and loss of VAT deduction rights.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate for goods exported outside the EU or qualifying intra-EU supplies upon proof of dispatch and destination outside France; offshore services subject to reverse charge mechanism and specific substantiation criteria.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of payment to non-EU recipient
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims result in full VAT liability, interest charges, fines up to 5% of unreported turnover, and potential criminal prosecution; retrospective audits trigger clawback of benefits with penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates under a fully convertible currency regime for the euro. Capital account transactions are generally permitted without prior approval for resident companies. Profit remittances to foreign shareholders are straightforward, subject to corporate tax compliance and beneficial ownership declarations. Hurdles are limited to standard KYC and source of funds verification for large amounts exceeding €100,000.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds to the Banque de France is required under French law. However, banks must verify the legitimacy of export receipts through supporting documentation such as commercial invoices, packing lists, and certificates of origin. Proceeds should ideally be collected within 180 days of shipment and recorded appropriately for tax purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasible for authorized fintechs under PSD2 and French EMI regulations, but offshore digital EMIs face legal constraints including potential authorization requirements and compliance with French data protection laws (GDPR).
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding with video KYC is permitted for SARL entities, but physical appearance of directors may be mandated for high-value accounts or complex structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media or sanctions exposure on beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive dossier including proof of clean criminal record, business registration certificates, export contracts, and bank references

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are routed via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'CAP' or 'EQTY'. Verification requires board resolutions, incorporation documents, and proof of source of funds. All transactions must be processed through French correspondent banks with full compliance to AML/CFT directives.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements utilize SWIFT MT103 for direct payments and Commercial Letters of Credit for secured settlements. Payments must be supported by export contracts, invoices, and shipping documents.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts (bilan and compte de résultat)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after shareholders' meeting approving accounts (typically by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to 10,000 EUR and administrative strike-off risk after 3 months of non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of corporate income tax return (déclaration de résultat)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 15 May following fiscal year-end (or 3 months with extension)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of 0.5% per month of tax due (max 80% of tax) and potential administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 3 months after year-end if ownership or control changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to 10,000 EUR and administrative sanctions for non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if annual turnover exceeds 800,000 EUR or total assets exceed 400,000 EUR

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual filing and update of beneficial ownership information to RCS

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small and medium-sized companies may qualify for a 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to ownership, turnover and capital conditions. Qualifying net income from patents and certain equivalent intellectual property may be taxed at an effective 10% rate. The French research tax credit generally equals 30% of eligible research expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold. Qualifying innovation expenditure may receive a separate reduced-rate credit subject to statutory limits. No general tax holiday applies to an ordinary SARL manufacturing ventilators.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward, subject to the annual utilization ceiling of EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Carryback is generally limited to the preceding financial year and is capped at the lower of the preceding year's profit and EUR 1 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD and annex 2065 bis-SD for corporate income tax, filed electronically through the French tax administration's professional online service or through an approved EDI-TDFC provider. Tax computation schedules generally include Form 2058-A-SD, Form 2058-B-SD and Form 2058-C-SD under the normal regime, or the 2033 series under the simplified regime.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return, with quarterly advance installments and a final balance payment where applicable
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on 31 December, the annual return is generally due on the second business day following 1 May of the following year. For a financial year ending on a date other than 31 December, the return is generally due within three months after the financial year-end. The filing calendar published by the French tax administration applies where the statutory date is adjusted. Corporate income tax installments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, with the final balance generally due by the fifteenth day of the fourth month following year-end, or by 15 May for a 31 December year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SARL form, registered office, SIREN number, principal business activity, financial year opening and closing dates, tax office and accounting regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the French SARL as the taxpayer. A non-resident shareholder is not entered as the taxpayer unless it itself operates a French taxable permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2065-SD, taxable result and tax liability section
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss, corporate income tax base, applicable rate, gross tax, tax credits, foreign tax credits where available, instalments and balance payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the French company's taxable result. Do not consolidate the foreign parent's worldwide income. Deductible related-party charges must satisfy French business-purpose, arm's-length and documentation requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Relevant distributions, deemed distributions, shareholder remuneration and other reportable profit allocations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record dividends and other distributions to foreign shareholders consistently with the accounting records and withholding tax filings. Treaty reductions do not eliminate the obligation to report the distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss adjusted for non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, timing differences, depreciation limits, provisions, financial expenses, transfer pricing adjustments and other French tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-parent accounting entries must be removed or separately reconciled unless legally attributable to the French entity. Intercompany charges require contracts, benefit evidence, allocation keys and arm's-length support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year tax loss, carried-forward losses, utilized losses, remaining losses and any carryback claim.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign group losses cannot be imported into the French SARL. French losses remain subject to the French utilization ceiling and may be restricted after a substantial change in business activity or a qualifying change in the entity's identity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable profit between current-year result, carried-forward losses, special regimes, credits and other tax components.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply only French statutory regimes and credits for which the SARL has supporting records. Foreign incentives or parent-company tax attributes are not entered in this schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual summary of related-party transactions, transaction categories, amounts, methods, counterparties and transfer pricing documentation status where the statutory threshold is met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report transactions with foreign group companies, including goods, royalties, technical services, financing, guarantees and cost allocations. Amounts must reconcile to the ledger, statutory accounts and Local File.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Research tax credit Form 2069-A-SD and related annexes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Eligible research expenditure, subcontracted research, personnel costs, depreciation, overheads, grants and calculated research tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only French-qualifying research activity and retain technical files, personnel records, timesheets, invoices and evidence of scientific uncertainty. Group financing or foreign R&D expenditure does not qualify merely because it benefits the French company.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% for deliberate non-compliance and potentially 80% for fraudulent maneuvers or abuse of rights. Late payment generally attracts a 5% surcharge plus late-payment interest, normally 0.20% per month. Inaccurate declarations may trigger tax reassessment, interest, penalties based on taxpayer conduct and criminal referral in serious cases.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate income tax installment and balance payment orders submitted electronically through the French professional tax account or an approved electronic payment channel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly installments and annual balance payment
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Installments are generally payable by 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December. The balance is generally payable by the fifteenth day of the fourth month following year-end, subject to the special deadline for a 31 December year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification, financial year and installment number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SARL's SIREN and tax account. The foreign shareholder's tax identification number is not a substitute for the French taxpayer reference.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year or estimated current-year corporate income tax liability, applicable credits and amount payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Estimate only the French SARL's liability. Recalculate installments where credits, losses or material changes in profitability make the statutory estimate inaccurate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax liability less installments, withholding credits and permitted tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the payment to the filed 2065 return and retain payment confirmations, bank references and tax-account statements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment may trigger a 5% surcharge and late-payment interest, generally 0.20% per month. Repeated payment failures may lead to collection measures, bank-account attachment, director liability in exceptional cases and criminal exposure where the conduct forms part of tax fraud or insolvency abuse.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% domestic withholding tax generally applies to dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident corporate recipient, subject to exemptions and treaty relief. Qualifying EU or EEA parent companies may obtain an exemption under the French implementation of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, generally requiring a qualifying participation, minimum holding period and anti-abuse compliance. Individual recipients may be subject to different domestic rates.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's competent foreign tax authority, confirm beneficial ownership and treaty entitlement, test limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose provisions where relevant, and retain evidence of the participation, holding period and absence of abusive arrangements. The French payer should apply the reduced treaty rate only where the applicable administrative conditions are satisfied; otherwise it should withhold at the domestic rate and the recipient may seek a refund using the prescribed French refund procedure. Dividend reporting and withholding returns must be filed through the applicable French tax channels. A treaty certificate does not by itself override anti-abuse, beneficial-ownership or substance requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties and similar payments to non-residents may generally be subject to a domestic withholding rate of 25%, subject to statutory exemptions, EU rules and treaty reductions. The applicable treaty rate commonly ranges from 0% to 15%, depending on the treaty and royalty category. Ordinary interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding tax, but exceptions may apply to payments in non-cooperative or low-tax situations, profit-participating instruments, certain related-party arrangements and anti-abuse cases. Treaty interest rates commonly range from 0% to 15%. French withholding, transfer pricing, thin-capitalization, beneficial-ownership and deductibility rules must be analyzed separately.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Master File and Local File documentation is generally mandatory where the French entity or French tax group has annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets of at least EUR 400 million, or where it is controlled by or controls an entity meeting that threshold, subject to statutory group and filing conditions. An annual transfer pricing declaration generally applies at lower thresholds, commonly where turnover or gross assets reach EUR 50 million or where controlled transactions exceed specified category thresholds, including the EUR 100,000 category threshold. Documentation should nevertheless be maintained below the formal threshold where material related-party transactions exist.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no single standalone economic substance regulation equivalent to the United Arab Emirates ESR regime. Substance is enforced through transfer pricing, permanent establishment, controlled foreign company, interest limitation, beneficial ownership, anti-abuse and principal-purpose rules. The French SARL should maintain genuine French functions, qualified personnel, premises or operational capacity appropriate to its activity, decision-making evidence, inventory and manufacturing records, customer and supplier management, and commercially justified intragroup arrangements. A French entity lacking operational substance may face denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization, transfer pricing adjustments, permanent establishment findings, withholding tax exposure and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing French sales, inflating deductible costs, fabricating invoices, omitting taxable distributions, deliberately understating inventory or filing a knowingly false corporate income tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, tax interest, conduct-based penalties generally up to 80%, and criminal tax fraud penalties that may include imprisonment for up to 5 years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000. Aggravated circumstances may increase exposure to up to 7 years' imprisonment and EUR 3 million, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and directors who personally participate in fraud may face criminal prosecution, personal fines, imprisonment and civil liability. Tax collection may be extended to a director whose serious and repeated management misconduct makes collection impossible. Travel restrictions are not an automatic tax-fraud sanction but may arise from judicial measures or other proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing manipulation and hidden profit distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Excessive royalties, management fees, financing charges, guarantees or purchase prices paid to foreign group companies without demonstrable benefit, functions, risk assumption or arm's-length support.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Addition of the excessive amount to French taxable income, potential withholding tax on recharacterized distributions, 40% or 80% penalties depending on conduct, late-payment interest, and possible documentation penalties. The French tax administration may apply a French taxable profit adjustment under the arm's-length principle.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal liability where they knowingly approve fictitious or abusive transactions, participate in fraud or cause insolvency. Ordinary transfer pricing adjustment does not automatically pierce limited liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared permanent establishment or disguised French activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting manufacturing, sales, installation, servicing or contract negotiation in France through a foreign company while treating the French SARL or personnel as an undisclosed agent or avoiding French taxable presence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive taxation of attributable French profits, corporate income tax, VAT, payroll and social charges, withholding obligations, interest and penalties. Deliberate concealment may constitute tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed for fraudulent concealment, payroll violations or insolvency-related misconduct. Civil veil piercing is exceptional and requires serious personal misconduct or statutory grounds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Transferring assets to a foreign parent, paying related parties while insolvent, stripping inventory or cash, preferring affiliates, or continuing operations while concealing inability to pay debts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Court-ordered clawback, extension of insolvency proceedings, director liability for all or part of the insufficiency of assets, management bans and possible criminal bankruptcy sanctions, including imprisonment and fines under the French Commercial Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil restitution, contribution to liabilities, disqualification from management and criminal prosecution. A travel ban is not automatic but judicial control or other criminal measures may restrict travel.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained government, distributor or intermediary funds, using opaque beneficial owners, structuring payments, routing proceeds through high-risk jurisdictions, or failing to investigate unusual Swift wires and related-party payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Suspicious transactions may be reportable to TRACFIN where the entity is within an obliged-profession category. Criminal money laundering may carry up to 5 years' imprisonment and EUR 375,000, with aggravated forms carrying higher penalties. Assets may be seized or confiscated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly facilitate laundering may be prosecuted personally, fined, imprisoned and subject to asset confiscation. Corporate limited liability does not protect intentional criminal participants.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Importing or selling invasive mechanical ventilators without required EU conformity assessment, CE marking, technical documentation, post-market surveillance, French registration or accurate customs and origin declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Product withdrawal, recall, prohibition of sale, customs detention, administrative fines, loss of market access and civil damages. False customs declarations may generate customs duties, penalties and criminal exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal liability for knowingly placing unsafe or non-compliant medical devices on the market, particularly where injury or death results. Civil claims may include compensation and restitution; travel bans are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Dividend distribution in breach of capital-maintenance rules
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits without approved accounts, distributing amounts exceeding distributable reserves, concealing accumulated losses, or paying dividends that impair legally protected capital or creditor interests.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unlawfully paid dividends, shareholder and director liability, accounting remediation and potential criminal sanctions for fictitious dividends or false corporate accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers approving unlawful distributions may face civil liability, management restrictions and criminal prosecution. Personal restitution may be ordered; limited liability does not protect directors from their own statutory breach.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining double books, recording fictitious sales or expenses, backdating contracts, manipulating production or inventory records, or concealing related-party transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, accounting penalties, civil damages, criminal penalties for false accounts or related offenses, and possible prohibition from managing a company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director or manager who orders, approves or knowingly tolerates false records may be personally prosecuted and may face fines, imprisonment, restitution and management disqualification.
